Ang endocrine system usa ka grupo sa mga glandula — sama sa pituitary, thyroid, adrenal, ug pancreas — nga naghimo sa mga hormone nga nagdumala sa lawas!

Sputnik 1 was the first! It was launched by the Soviet Union to orbit Earth.
copy.tl:
Ano ang unang gawang-taong satellite na umikot sa Earth?

Ang Sputnik 1 ang una! Inilunsad ito ng Soviet Union para umikot sa Earth.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang unang hinimo-sa-tawo nga satellite nga milibot sa Yuta?

Ang Sputnik 1 ang una! Gilunsad kini sa Soviet Union aron milibot sa Yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Voyager 1 was the first spacecraft to leave our solar system and enter interstellar space
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies including telescopes and space probes
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a space probe (Voyager 1) and its achievement, but it does not explain how modern research uses space technologies such as telescopes and space probes. It only states a historical fact about a probe leaving the solar system, which is not direct instructional support for the competency's skill of explaining the use of space technologies in research.

copy.en:
What was the first spacecraft to leave our solar system?

Voyager 1 was the first spacecraft to leave our solar system and enter interstellar space, and it did this in 2012!
copy.tl:
Ano ang unang spacecraft na nakalabas sa ating solar system?

Ang Voyager 1 ang unang spacecraft na nakalabas sa ating solar system at pumasok sa interstellar space noong 2012!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang unang spacecraft nga nakagawas sa atong solar system?

Ang Voyager 1 ang unang spacecraft nga nakagawas sa atong solar system ug misulod sa interstellar space niadtong 2012!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: caught fresh from the sea or a fishpond
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fish coming from the sea or a fishpond, which touches on habitat, but it does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat, nor does it teach the classification skill. Format-required competency is not met.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: packed with protein
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes fish as a protein-rich food but does not identify basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The fish you see at the market is packed with protein, caught fresh from the sea or a fishpond.
copy.tl: Ang isdang ibinebenta sa palengke ay puno ng protina, hango sa dagat o sa palaisdaan.
copy.bis: Ang isda nga gibaligya sa merkado puno sa protina, gikan sa dagat o sa isdaan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The outrigger floats on each side of the banca to keep it steady.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the function of an outrigger (stability) but does not describe any physical properties of solid materials such as hardness, shininess, or stretchability. It only mentions that the outrigger floats, which is a behavior, not a material property.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It stops the boat from tipping over even with big waves!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stability against tipping, which relates to movement, but it does not explore or describe factors affecting movement such as size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture. The outrigger's role in preventing tipping is not presented as an investigation of these factors.

copy.en: The outrigger floats on each side of the banca to keep it steady. It stops the boat from tipping over even with big waves!
copy.tl: Lumulutang ang katig sa magkabilang gilid ng bangka para panatilihin itong matatag. Pinipigilan nito ang bangka na tumaob kahit may malalaking alon!
copy.bis: Naglutaw ang katig sa duha ka kilid sa bangka aron magpabiling lig-on kini. Mapugngan niini ang bangka nga motakilid bisan adunay dagkong balod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists sort creatures into kingdoms by asking: Is it one cell or many? Does it have a nucleus? Does it eat, absorb, or make its own food?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the importance of the six-kingdom system and the three-domain system of classification of living things
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses assigning organisms to kingdoms using general questions, but does not describe the six-kingdom system, the three-domain system, or their importance. It only touches on the broad concept of classification, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists sort creatures into kingdoms by asking: Is it one cell or many? Does it have a nucleus? Does it eat, absorb, or make its own food?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions classification into kingdoms but does not use a table, does not name the specific groups (plants, animals, microorganisms) or their subgroups, and does not classify based on the similar characteristics listed in the competency. It is only related to the general idea of classification.

copy.en: Scientists sort creatures into kingdoms by asking: Is it one cell or many? Does it have a nucleus? Does it eat, absorb, or make its own food?
copy.tl: Ini-uuri ng mga siyentista ang mga nilalang sa kingdom sa pagtatanong: Isang selula ba ito o marami? May nucleus ba? Kumakain, sumisipsip, o gumagawa ba ng sariling pagkain?
copy.bis: Giklasipika sa mga siyentista ang mga binuhat sa kingdom pinaagi sa pagpangutana: Usa ba ka selula o daghan? Adunay nucleus ba? Mokaon, mosuyop, o maghimo ba og kaugalingong pagkaon?

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The metal's ELECTRONS jump to higher energy and release light as they fall back!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains electron energy transitions causing flame colors, but does not describe the nucleus or electron shells, nor does it ask students to draw the atom's structure. It only touches on electrons, which is a related concept but not direct instruction for drawing the atom.

copy.en:
Why do flame-test colors appear?

The metal's ELECTRONS jump to higher energy and release light as they fall back!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumalabas ang mga kulay sa flame test?

Dahil ang mga ELEKTRON ng metal ay umaakyat sa mas mataas na energy at naglalabas ng liwanag pagbalik!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mogawas ang mga kolor sa flame test?

Tungod kay ang ELEKTRON sa metal mosaka sa mas taas nga energy ug mogawas ang kahayag pagbalik!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it gives a gorgeous GOLD (yellow) flame color
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the electron structure of an atom determines its position on the periodic table
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a flame-test color for iron. It does not explain electron structure or how electron structure determines an element's position on the periodic table. The flame color is a peripheral fact about electron transitions, not instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: When you put iron (Fe) in a flame test, it doesn't just spark—it gives a gorgeous GOLD (yellow) flame color! It looks like real treasure.
copy.tl: Kapag nilagay mo ang iron (Fe) sa isang flame test, hindi lang ito tumalima—nagbibigay ito ng magandang GINTO o dilaw (gold-yellow) na kulay sa apoy! Mukhang tunay na yaman.
copy.bis: Kung ibutang nimo ang iron (Fe) sa flame test, dili lang kini moesparka—mohatag kini ug nindot nga BULAWAN o dalag (gold-yellow) nga kolor sa kalayo! Murag tinuod nga bahandi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Flamingos munch on algae, tiny shrimp, and other small water critters for their meals!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides factual diet information for flamingos (algae and shrimp) but does not explicitly group the animal into herbivore, carnivore, or omnivore, nor does it teach the classification skill. It supplies background knowledge that could be used in a grouping activity, but does not directly support the competency's action of grouping animals by food type.

copy.en: Flamingos munch on algae, tiny shrimp, and other small water critters for their meals!
copy.tl: Kumakain ang flamingo ng lumot, maliliit na hipon, at iba pang maliliit na hayop sa tubig!
copy.bis: Ang flamingo mokaon ug lumot, gagmayng pasayan, ug ubang gagmayng mananap sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Standing on one leg is easy for a flamingo
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a leg but does not describe outer body parts or identify their role in moving or gathering food. It focuses on the ease of balancing, not on the structure or function of the leg.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Standing on one leg is easy for a flamingo
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe how an animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it mention adaptation, mimicry, or camouflage. It only states that standing on one leg requires little effort.

copy.en:
Why doesn't a flamingo get tired standing on one leg?

Standing on one leg is easy for a flamingo — it barely uses any muscle or effort to hold that pose!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi napapagod ang flamingo?

Madali lang para sa flamingo ang tumayo sa isang paa — halos walang kalamnan o lakas na ginagamit dito!
copy.bis:
Ngano wala gikapoy ang flamingo?

Sayon ra sa flamingo ang pagtindog sa usa ka tiil — halos walay kaunuran o kusog nga gigamit niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A flamingo's pink feathers actually come from the food it eats
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that flamingo color comes from food, but does not group animals by diet (herbivore, carnivore, omnivore) or teach classification by food type. It only touches on food as a cause of color, not on dietary categories.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A flamingo's pink feathers actually come from the food it eats
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions feathers (an outer body part) but does not describe outer body parts or their role in movement or gathering food. The focus is on color source, not on body part function.

copy.en:
Why are flamingos pink?

A flamingo's pink feathers actually come from the food it eats, not from how it was born!
copy.tl:
Bakit rosas ang balahibo ng flamingo?

Ang kulay-rosas na balahibo ng flamingo ay galing pala sa kanilang kinakain, hindi sa pagkakapanganak nila!
copy.bis:
Nganong rosas ang balhibo sa flamingo?

Ang rosas nga balhibo sa flamingo gikan diay sa ilang gikaon, dili sa pagkahimugso nila!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: floats because it's made of light wood and hollow inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains buoyancy and stability of a bangka (light wood, hollow interior, outriggers), not the movement of objects or factors like size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture affecting motion. Floating/sinking is not movement as intended by this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: made of light wood and hollow inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions 'light wood' and 'hollow inside,' which are physical properties, but the competency asks for describing physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card does not describe the wood's properties directly; it uses them to explain floating, so it only touches the same vocabulary.

copy.en: The Filipino fishermen's bangka floats because it's made of light wood and hollow inside. Its outriggers (katig) on the sides keep it from tipping and sinking!
copy.tl: Lumulutang ang bangka ng mga mangingisdang Pilipino dahil gawa ito sa magaang kahoy at guwang sa loob. Ang mga katig sa gilid ay pumipigil sa pagtagilid at paglubog!
copy.bis: Molutaw ang bangka sa mga Pilipino nga mangingisda tungod kay hinimo sa gaan nga kahoy ug guwang sa sulod. Ang mga katig sa kilid mopugong sa pagkatumba ug paglubog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That submerged part pushes aside enough water to keep them floating.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why objects float partway (buoyancy), but the competency is about factors affecting the movement of objects (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). Floating is a static condition, not movement, and the card does not address how these factors affect motion.

copy.en:
Do all floating things stay completely on top of the water?

Nope! Things like ice or wood have part underwater. That submerged part pushes aside enough water to keep them floating.
copy.tl:
Lahat ba ng lumulutang ay nasa ibabaw lang?

Hindi! Ang yelo o kahoy ay may bahaging nakalubog. Ang bahaging iyon ang nagtutulak ng sapat na tubig para manatiling nakalutang.
copy.bis:
Tanan ba nga naglutaw anaa lang sa ibabaw?

Dili! Ang yelo o kahoy adunay bahin nga nilunod. Ang bahina mao ang motulak ug igong tubig aron magpabilin nga naglutaw.
